title_hint: Casual architecture chat with a friend about a local transcription app, no commitments

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay so I wanted your take on the, the architecture thing before I go further.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sure. Is this the notes app?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yeah. So right now transcription runs whisper locally, and then the summary goes to some API. I'm wondering if I should run the LLM locally too.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: What model, like a seven b?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yeah, seven or eight b, quantized. But on a normal laptop it's, it's slow, like thirty seconds for a long meeting, if you're lucky.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I mean, honestly, I'd keep the API as default and offer local as an option.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's, that's what I was thinking. Though maybe I should just try it first and see.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Also, you could, you know, maybe do a plugin system someday. Like people write their own templates.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yeah, someday. That's a v2 thing, totally.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: What about speaker labels? Do you have diarization?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: No, only me versus everyone else, mic versus system audio. It's simple but it works surprisingly well.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Right, that's smart actually. Oh, did you see the, uh, new Whisper turbo thing?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Not yet. I should probably benchmark it at some point, but, honestly, no promises.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Ha. Anyway, how's the other thing, the design studio, are you swamped?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Kind of. Paris is, it's raining nonstop, and we had a client call that went sideways.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Ugh. Weather here is the same. Did you ever get your bike fixed?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: No, the shop wanted two weeks. I'll probably just buy a new one.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Classic. Okay, so back to the app, are you gonna open source it?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yeah, it's MIT already. Fork of something else, so I have to keep their copyright in.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Makes sense. I could have a look at the code if you want, but I'm slammed until, like, December.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: No pressure. Seriously.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Alright. Let's grab a beer when you're back in town.

non_action_traps: Maybe try a local LLM first and see (tentative idea)
Plugin system for templates someday (v2 idea)
Benchmark the new Whisper turbo at some point, no promises (explicitly not a commitment)
